cars.variant: GSX turbo AWD, five-speed manual — 1990 US factory reference
cars.specification_market: 1990 US-market first-generation Eclipse GSX, five-speed manual. Original Mitsubishi four-page GSX AWD brochure, hosted by ImportArchive: all four public low-resolution scans actually inspected. Factory advertised 195 hp at 6000 rpm and 203 lb-ft at 3000 rpm, 1997 cc, DOHC four valves per cylinder, multi-point injection and air-to-air intercooled turbo. Native hp/lb-ft retained without asserting an unstated SAE rating convention or metric conversion. Full-time AWD uses a viscous-coupled centre differential; 50:50 is the stated normal-running split, not an immutable split. Japan GSR-4 naming/calibration, later engines, automatic figures, tuned output and acceleration claims are not imported. The rear torque-control suspension link is not evidence of active rear torque vectoring or a rear limited-slip differential. Japanese Mitsubishi programme, assembled by Diamond-Star Motors in Normal, Illinois. High-resolution 1990 scans remain donation-gated and were not accessed.
cars.summary: The original Eclipse turbo/AWD performance programme combined an intercooled twin-cam four with full-time four-wheel traction in a compact sports coupe. Its viscous-coupled centre differential and independent rear suspension distinguish the selected GSX from ordinary front-drive trim. Count the first-generation Diamond-Star road family once, including Eclipse, Eagle Talon and Plymouth Laser aliases; badges, transmissions and model years add no extra entries.

cars.generation: Second-generation Eclipse / Talon shared Diamond-Star production-road coupe family
cars.variant: GSX turbo AWD, five-speed manual — 1995 US factory reference
cars.specification_market: 1995 US-market second-generation Eclipse GSX, standard five-speed manual. Original Mitsubishi MMSA-ADV-5618 brochure, copyright 1994: actual high-resolution pages 14–15 inspected. Turbo/intercooled 2.0-litre DOHC 16-valve four, multi-point injection, 210 hp at 6000 rpm and 214 lb-ft at 3000 rpm. These are native advertised US figures; no unstated SAE convention, Japanese PS value or inferred metric torque/displacement conversion is supplied. Automatic is optional and has a different 205-hp / 220-lb-ft rating, not selected. AWD with centre and rear limited-slip differentials is standard on GSX; ABS is optional. GSX manual tyres are 215/55VR16, not the automatic size. The 2877-lb curb weight shown is GS-T manual, not GSX, and is omitted. No NA GS/RS Chrysler engine figures or Talon test measurements are copied. 1995 is the chosen US model year, not the Japanese launch date; Japanese-market second-generation specifications differ. The family photograph depicts a later facelift, not an exact 1995 body.
cars.summary: The second Eclipse generation substantially renewed the Diamond-Star performance coupe with four-wheel independent multi-link suspension and a 210-hp intercooled turbo manual reference. The GSX paired that chassis with AWD and centre/rear limited-slip differentials, sustaining the programme’s distinctive high-performance role. Count this generation once across Eclipse and Eagle Talon; badges, GS/GS-T/GSX grades, facelifts, gearboxes and Spyder bodies do not supply additional entries.
